name: Question 8
problem:
A curve is defined by the parametric equations

$$
x={e}^{t}\operatorname{sin}⁡(t),\,y={e}^{t}\operatorname{cos}⁡(t),\,0\le t\le 2\pi .
$$

Determine the values of $t$ at which the tangent to the curve is horizontal. Do not round the answers.

In **ascending order**, the tangent to the curve is horizontal at $t=$
{{field-1}}
and $t=$
{{field-2}}.
worked_solution:
The slope $m$ of a tangent line to a curve defined parametrically is given by

$$
m=\frac{{y}^{′}(t)}{{x}^{′}(t)}.
$$

The tangent line is horizontal if ${y}^{′}(t)=0$ while ${x}^{′}(t)\ne 0.$

So, we first find the derivatives of $x$ and $y:$

$$
{x}^{′}(t)={e}^{t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)+\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)),\,{y}^{′}(t)={e}^{t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)-\operatorname{sin}⁡(t))
$$

Solving ${y}^{′}(t)=0$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)-\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)) & =0 \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(t)-\operatorname{sin}⁡(t) & =0 \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(t) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(t) \\ \frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)}{\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)} & =1 \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡(t) & =1 \\ t & =\frac{\pi }{4},\frac{5\pi }{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we note that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{4}) & ={e}^{\frac{\pi }{4}}[\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})+\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})]=\sqrt{2}{e}^{\frac{\pi }{4}}\ne 0, \\ {x}^{′}(\frac{5\pi }{4}) & ={e}^{\frac{5\pi }{4}}[\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{5\pi }{4})+\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{5\pi }{4})]=-\sqrt{2}{e}^{\frac{5\pi }{4}}\ne 0,\end{aligned}
$$

which confirms that the tangent to the curve is indeed horizontal at $t=\frac{\pi }{4}$ and $t=\frac{5\pi }{4}.$

EXPLANATION

The slope m of a tangent line to a curve defined parametrically is given by m=y′(t)x′(t). The tangent line is horizontal if y′(t)=0 while x′(t)≠0.

So, we first find the derivatives of x and y: x′(t)=et(sin⁡(t)+cos⁡(t)),y′(t)=et(cos⁡(t)−sin⁡(t))

Solving y′(t)=0 gives et(cos⁡(t)−sin⁡(t))=0cos⁡(t)−sin⁡(t)=0sin⁡(t)=cos⁡(t)sin⁡(t)cos⁡(t)=1tan⁡(t)=1t=π4,5π4.

Now, we note that x′(π4)=eπ4[sin⁡(π4)+cos⁡(π4)]=2eπ4≠0,x′(5π4)=e5π4[sin⁡(5π4)+cos⁡(5π4)]=−2e5π4≠0, which confirms that the tangent to the curve is indeed horizontal at t=π4 and t=5π4.
